Reads the unit's script control block and, for each of +998h, +99Ch and +9A0h that is not exactly zero, clamps it with 'if (-1.0f <= v) { if (1.0f < v) v = 1.0f; } else v = -1.0f' (00D7A260, 00D7A24C) and commits it into the plan slots at +284h, +29Ch and +290h with the flag set and the timer cleared (0099D5D8, 0099D63A, 0099D69C); +9A4h takes the same clamp and feeds a heading after 007B4ED0. Slots are read as flag ? pending : committed (0099E996, 0099EABF). It writes no unit field. See docs/UNIT_COMMAND_PRODUCERS.md. | Packet cc8_torpedo_moveto_tick follow-up, read-only: this routine is the ONLY producer of a bot plane's throttle. The plan's throttle slot is index 0 of five, so its desired is plan+278h and its active byte plan+27Ch (base plan+274h, stride 0Ch, per docs/PILOT_PLAN_SLOT_PIPELINE.md). An exhaustive store census over 278h returns 65 sites image-wide and four of them are here, all on the ESI that 0099D305 MOV ESI,ECX makes the plan: 0099D399 the centred-stick arm, which sets yaw, pitch, roll and air brake to 0.0 with their active bytes and modes and the throttle to [00D7A24C] = 1.0, raising the slot's own active byte at 0099D3A1 - the pair that proves the record is the plan, since only the plan has it; 0099D8CF the speed-hold arm, entered when a mode equals 1 and a demand exceeds plan+2B4h, writing the air brake beside it at 0099D8DD; 0099DC31 a floor through 00415550 BSP_Math_MaxFloatByRef; and 0099DC8F a CEILING that pins the throttle to [00CE3D30] = 0.6. So the native cuts a bot's throttle in the planner, not in any task state - no task arm writes the slot, which is why the attack-run 009D07B0, aim 009D15F0 and move-to 009C18C0 ticks all came up empty. The demands themselves (XMM0 at 0099D8C6 and 0099DC8A) are unread. docs/PILOT_BOT_THROTTLE_ARM.md. | Packet cc8_pilot_throttle_demands, read-only. The four throttle writes are FOUR ARMS with four gates, and two are ground handling - which CORRECTS the previous record's reading that the native cuts a bot's throttle to 0.6. 0099D8FD CMP dword [EDX+900h],5 with EDX = plan+2F0h, then 0099D904 JNZ 0099DC9E, puts both the demand at 0099DC31 and the cap at 0099DC8F inside unit+900h == 5, a ground-roll state; a plane in free flight jumps past both, so the 0.6 at 00CE3D30 is a TAXI cap. The centred-stick arm 0099D399 is gated on plan+26Ch == 2 (0099D309) and the per-slot byte at [unit + 9C2h + 8*[00F876B8]] set on both plan+2F0h (0099D329) and plan+270h (0099D345, with 0099D33D rejecting null); it writes every axis to 0.0 with its active byte and mode and the throttle to 1.0. The one-shot 0099D8CF is gated on plan+2D8h != 0 at 0099D7A5 - the jump at 0099D7AF is what leaves 0.001f from 00D7A23C in XMM0 - then plan+2D8h == 1 at 0099D8C1 and 0.001f > plan+2B4h at 0099D8C6; XMM0 is that CONSTANT and not a demand, because 0099D8BF JMP 0099D8F7 means the arm is reached only by those jumps. 0.001f is below the 0.01f thrust gate at 007DB76C, so it switches the engine off, writes the air brake and clears plan+2D8h at 0099D8EB - the only throttle write a plane in state 7 can reach besides the centred-stick arm. The ground demand is one signed value seeded from the slot at 0099D977-0099D998, accumulated at 0099DBC3, clamped into [-1,1] by 00415690 at 0099DBF4 and split by two 00415550 calls: throttle = max(0.001f, d) at 0099DC31 and air brake = max(0.0f, -d) at 0099DC4B. Its increment chain 0099D9A3-0099DBAB is unread. docs/PILOT_BOT_THROTTLE_DEMANDS.md. | Packet cc8_pilot_throttle_cut_raiser: CORRECTION to this record's own previous entry. That entry says both the demand at 0099DC31 and the cap at 0099DC8F are inside unit+900h == 5. True for the CAP, which 0099D911 JZ 0099DC7A reaches only from inside the state branch. FALSE for the demand: 0099D8CD JBE 0099D924 jumps to an address PAST the state test at 0099D8FD, so whenever the one-shot plan+2D8h is 1 and the desired speed plan+2B4h is at or above 0.001f, the demand block runs in ANY flight state and writes the throttle and air brake at 0099DC31 and 0099DC4B. plan+2B4h is a DESIRED SPEED, not an abstract threshold: 009C1850 BSP_BotStateMoveTo_SetDesiredSpeed writes it at 009C189A and raises plan+2D8h at 009C18A7 in the same routine, unconditionally. And 0099D769 LEA EBP,[ESI+2B8h] makes plan+2B8h the reference the demand divides 007D99C0's forward speed by at 0099D9A3, with 0099D970 maxing 0099D95C's interpolation into it - so the demand's input is a speed ratio, measured over reference. docs/PILOT_THROTTLE_CUT_RAISER.md. | Packet cc8_pilot_throttle_increment, read-only: the ground demand's increment chain 0099D99E-0099DBC7 is a PROPORTIONAL SPEED CONTROLLER. 0099D99E takes 007D99C0's measured forward speed and 0099D9A3 divides it by plan+2B8h; 0099DA52/0099DA58 subtract that ratio from the desired speed plan+2B4h, so the error is DESIRED MINUS MEASURED and a bot flying too fast gets a negative increment that 0099DC46's max(0,-d) turns into air brake. 0099DAC8 subtracts a correction formed at 0099DA97-0099DAC4 as (unit vtable+38h - 0042B2F0 over the vec3 at unit+AE0h) * the double 20.0 at 00CE3D88 * the pending magnitude. 0099DB9E maps the error through InterpolateClamped(-6.9444 [00D1F3DC], -2.0 [00CE7D7C], +6.9444 [00D0686C], +2.0 [00CE3958]), whose endpoints are minus and plus 25 km/h; 0099DBB1 scales only the positive side by the double 0.6 at 00CEFF98; 0099DBBF scales by the pending magnitude; 0099DBC3 accumulates onto the seed. The [-1,1] clamp at 0099DBF4 is on the ACCUMULATED DEMAND, not the increment. There is NO frame-time factor: [ESP+6Ch] is written at 0099D7E8-0099D81E as |slot value - plan+274h|, so the increment is scaled by how far the slot has already been asked to move and is ZERO for a slot whose desired equals its current - every slot out of 0099B450's reset. A dead band at 0099DB29-0099DB56 skips the increment when |error| <= 0.83333 (00D09450), ratio >= 1.0, desired/|ratio| <= 1.5 (00CE380C) and 0.5 (00CE3800) > desired/|ratio| all hold. 0099DB65 mins plan+2ECh against 0.16 (00E0E2F0) just before the map. docs/PILOT_THROTTLE_CUT_RAISER.md. | Packet cc8_attack_run_descent, read-only: the pitch path is complete, and NOTHING in it stops a DEG(60) dive for an aircraft level and on heading. Pitch mode 2, 0099DCE0-0099DD4E: 0099DCF1 loads the held pitch unit+C84h, 0099DD35 forms an increment from the unit's cached speed against DEG(5) [00CEDF5C] and DEG(20) [00CE398C], 0099DD42 adds them, and 0099DD4C JBE keeps the COMMANDED value when it is at or below that sum - so a dive command, being far below, passes through untouched and mode 2 limits only a climb. 0099DCD4 demotes mode 2 to mode 1 when the speed falls below the float 2.7778 at 00D1F3D8, 10 km/h, which no flying aircraft reaches. The nose-up floor, 0099E490-0099E512: 0099E496/0099E49A form |bank| / class+25Ch TurnRoll, 0099E4AA clamps it at 1.0, 0099E4CC multiplies by the heading ramp, 0099E4DC scales by the double 2.5 at 00CE3DE0, and 0099E4FE JBE takes the floor only when it EXCEEDS the target, so plan+2BCh = max(target, PitchTurnMaxPitch - 2.5*(1-q)). With the authored PitchTurnMaxPitch of DEG(6) that floor is -2.395 rad level and on heading, 1.35 radians below the DEG(60) cap at 00D05AAC, and only reaches +DEG(6) in a hard banked turn past DEG(50) of heading error. So the image produces the same -1.0472 rad this reconstruction measured, and src/plane_ai_control.cpp matches it stage for stage. docs/ATTACK_RUN_DESCENT.md. | Packet cc8_done_state, docs/BOMBER_AFTER_TASK.md 6c: entry gate A (0099D309-0099D3C2) is the NEUTRAL PLAN and returns, skipping the remaining ~1400 instructions. It needs FOUR conditions, not just the mode byte: cmd+26Ch==2 (0099D309), unit[9C2h+idx*8]!=0 (0099D329), cmd+270h!=0 (0099D33D) and target[9C2h+idx*8]!=0 (0099D345), idx=word[00F876B8]. unit[idx*8+9C2h] is the published copy of unit+520h (007CDCD0). tools/callsite_census.py gives exactly two call sites, 00999907 and 009999AA, BOTH inside 009998A0, whose own entry gate returns at 009999B0 on a SUPERSET of gate A, so gate A can only fire when the mode byte was written during the current tick by the state tick. 0099EA84 is the second reader and tests !=0, not ==2.
